name: Sony PlayStation Vita family
summary: Explore PS Vita OLED, Slim and PSTV hardware and the firmware-limited routes into homebrew: HENlo on 3.65/3.68/3.74, then Ensō on 3.60 or 3.65, subject to the factory-firmware floor.

specs.storage: Proprietary Vita memory card; 1 GB internal storage on PCH-2000

variants.storage: Proprietary Vita memory card only; no usable internal storage for games
variants.notes: PCH-1000 OLED model (2011 Japan, 2012 West). PCH-1100 is the 3G variant. h-encore² requires a memory card on this model.

specs.media: 5-inch 960x544 OLED; PS Vita game cards; Wi-Fi, 3G on PCH-1100

variants.storage: 1 GB internal storage plus memory card
variants.notes: PCH-2000 LCD model (2013). Lighter body with micro-USB charging. Internal storage can hold the jailbreak files without a memory card.

specs.media: 5-inch 960x544 LCD; PS Vita game cards; Wi-Fi

variants.notes: PSTV (2013-2014). TV-output variant with no screen or battery; runs Vita software subject to a title whitelist.

specs.media: HDMI output; PS Vita game cards; Wi-Fi

homebrew.name: HENlo
homebrew.summary: Current userland entry in the Vita Hacks Guide. It is not persistent, needs an internet connection on the console, and installs HENkaku and VitaDeploy.

compatibility.note: HENlo is compatible with these firmware versions. It does not remain installed after a reboot.

requirements: PS Vita or PSTV on firmware 3.65, 3.68 or 3.74.
An internet connection on the console.
A PSN-linked account is not required for HENlo.
warnings: HENlo is not persistent; re-run it after every cold boot unless Ensō is installed.
Do not let the console sleep during the 3.65 install.

homebrew.name: Ensō (HENkaku Ensō)
homebrew.firmware: Installed on 3.60 or 3.65; the current flow installs 3.65
homebrew.summary: Permanent boot-time CFW for Vita. The guide's current flow reaches it through HENlo and VitaDeploy's Quick 3.65 Install; manual install pages cover 3.60 and 3.65.

compatibility.note: Ensō is installed on 3.60 or 3.65. The current flow installs 3.65; manual pages cover both.

requirements: A jailbroken console with HENkaku or VitaDeploy.
For the current flow, HENlo on 3.65/3.68/3.74 followed by VitaDeploy's Quick 3.65 Install.
warnings: The guide calls the mod permanent and says there is no recovery if it fails.
Upstream warns that a bad install can perma-brick the console unless an eMMC dump was taken first.
Factory firmware above 3.65 blocks the downgrade to 3.60/3.65.

homebrew.name: VitaDeploy
homebrew.firmware: Toolbox for jailbroken Vitas; installs 3.60/3.65/3.68 and 3.65 + Ensō
homebrew.summary: Setup toolbox bundling VitaShell, sd2vita mount/format, firmware updater/downgrader, taiHEN setup, internal-memory unlock and app installs.

compatibility.note: Runs on a jailbroken console; no separate firmware matrix published beyond the firmware presets it downloads.

requirements: A jailbroken Vita or PSTV.
Internet access for the 3.65 quick install.
warnings: Do not let the console sleep during the 3.65 install.
Answer No to the internal-memory transfer prompt on reboot, per the guide.

homebrew.name: modoru
homebrew.firmware: Requires HENkaku or h-encore on 3.60-3.74; floor is the factory firmware
homebrew.summary: Downgrader for Vita. It can go down only to the firmware the console shipped with; devices whose factory firmware is above 3.65 cannot reach 3.60/3.65 for Ensō.

compatibility.note: Requires HENkaku or h-encore on 3.60-3.74. The floor is the factory firmware; a device with factory firmware above 3.65 cannot be downgraded to 3.60/3.65.

requirements: HENkaku or h-encore running on 3.60-3.74.
Memory card or internal storage, battery at least 50%, plugins disabled.
warnings: Downgrading below the factory firmware is not possible.
Memory-card failures are a common cause of broken installs.

homebrew.name: h-encore²
homebrew.summary: Historical jailbreak for Vita. Superseded in the current guide by HENlo, but still documented with its own firmware range.

compatibility.note: Upstream states support for firmware 3.65-3.74. On a phat OLED a memory card is mandatory; a PSN-linked account and about 270 MB free space are required.

requirements: PS Vita or PSTV on firmware 3.65-3.74.
On phat OLED models, a Vita memory card.
A PSN-linked account and about 270 MB free space.
warnings: Superseded by HENlo in the current guide.
Memory cards are discontinued and expensive.

homebrew.name: h-encore
homebrew.summary: Legacy jailbreak for Vita. Listed for completeness; not the recommended route.

compatibility.note: Legacy jailbreak; upstream states these exact versions.

requirements: PS Vita or PSTV on firmware 3.65, 3.67 or 3.68.
warnings: Legacy route; follow the guide's current flow instead.

homebrew.name: taiHEN
homebrew.firmware: Plugin framework set up by HENkaku or VitaDeploy; no firmware-specific list
homebrew.summary: Plugin framework for Vita. Plugins load at boot once configured through HENkaku or VitaDeploy.

compatibility.note: Set up by HENkaku or VitaDeploy; firmware support follows the jailbreak route used.

requirements: A jailbroken console with HENkaku or VitaDeploy.

homebrew.name: VitaShell
homebrew.firmware: File manager installed with VitaDeploy; no firmware-specific list
homebrew.summary: The usual file manager for moving files onto a jailbroken Vita.

compatibility.note: Application prerequisites are documented; firmware support follows the jailbreak route used.

requirements: A jailbroken Vita or PSTV.

homebrew.name: sd2vita
homebrew.firmware: MicroSD adapter mount and format support in VitaDeploy
homebrew.summary: Mounts a microSD card through an sd2vita adapter. VitaDeploy provides mount and format support; an adapter and microSD card are needed.

compatibility.note: Hardware adapter and mount; firmware support follows the jailbreak route used.

requirements: An sd2vita adapter and a microSD card.
VitaDeploy for mount and format.
warnings: Back up before formatting or repointing the storage mount.

homebrew.name: Sony PS Vita system software update and reinstall
homebrew.summary: Sony's official instructions for updating or reinstalling Vita system software in Safe Mode. Reinstalling requires the official PUP and a memory card.

compatibility.note: Official Vita recovery and update track shared by the whole family; reinstall does not accept older firmware.

requirements: Official PUP and a memory card; use Safe Mode as Sony documents.
warnings: Safe Mode reinstall erases console data.
Reinstalling does not downgrade the console.

homebrew.name: Vita firmware downgrade status - factory firmware floor
homebrew.firmware: No downgrade below the console's factory firmware
homebrew.summary: Records the documented Vita downgrade limit: modoru can only reach the factory firmware, so a console manufactured above 3.65 cannot reach 3.60/3.65 for Ensō.

compatibility.note: modoru can only reach the factory firmware. A device with factory firmware above 3.65 cannot be downgraded to 3.60/3.65.

warnings: Check the factory firmware before buying a used console for CFW.
An archived older PUP is not a downgrade method.

homebrew.name: Adrenaline
homebrew.firmware: Requires taiHEN (HENkaku/Enso); the changelog names 3.65, 3.67 and 3.68 support, but no current firmware matrix is published.
homebrew.summary: Modifies the official PSP emulator with taiHEN so it runs a PSP 6.61 custom firmware. It adds PS1 and PSP game launching, savestates, screen filters and a recovery menu.

compatibility.note: README and changelog describe taiHEN-based installs and 3.65/3.67/3.68 support; no current model/firmware matrix.

requirements: A Vita or PSTV with taiHEN installed (HENkaku or Enso).
VitaShell to install the VPK, and the PSP 6.61 firmware downloaded by the app.
warnings: PSP games and the 6.61 firmware are not bundled; the app downloads the firmware on first launch.
Without Enso, the README documents a double-launch workaround after each reboot.
homebrew.availability: Open source (GPL-3.0); VPK releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: VitaDB Downloader
homebrew.firmware: Requires a jailbroken Vita with taiHEN; the app itself has no firmware matrix.
homebrew.summary: The official client for VitaDB, the Vita homebrew database. It searches, downloads and installs homebrew VPKs and their data files on the console.

compatibility.note: Requires taiHEN and network access; no project firmware matrix.

requirements: A jailbroken Vita or PSTV with taiHEN.
A Wi-Fi connection for the catalogue and downloads.
warnings: Only installs homebrew listed by VitaDB; review each app before running it.
homebrew.availability: Open source; VPK releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: VitaGrafix
homebrew.firmware: Requires taiHEN; the plugin has no firmware matrix of its own.
homebrew.summary: A taiHEN plugin that changes the resolution and FPS cap of Vita games, with a separate community patchlist per title.

compatibility.note: Plugin requires taiHEN; no firmware matrix is published.

requirements: A Vita with taiHEN and a plugin loader.
The VitaGrafix patchlist for the games you want to patch.
warnings: Resolution and frame-rate patches can cause slowdowns or instability in some titles.
homebrew.availability: Open source (GPL-3.0); releases and patchlist published by the project.
